title: Runs But Never Walks
prompt: I run but never walk. I have a mouth but never talk. I have a head but never weep. I have a bed but never sleep.
hints: Think of each clue as a double meaning. 'Run' doesn't have to mean legs.
What natural thing has a mouth, a head, and a bed — but none of them are anatomical?
solution_lede:
Each line plays on the double meanings of familiar words:

A river *runs* (flows) but never walks. It has a *mouth* (where it meets the sea) but never talks. It has a *head* (source) but never weeps. It has a *bed* (the ground it flows over) but never sleeps.

The answer is a river.

solution_steps.body: Runs = flows. A river runs downstream constantly.
Mouth = the point where a river meets the sea or a lake.
Head = the source (headwaters) of a river. Bed = the ground beneath it.
